nodes.text: And whatever punishments I pass over, may he suffer those too;
may that man be more wretched than my wit [can devise]!
And so that prayers cursing a feigned name may not harm less,
or move the great gods less:
I curse him whom my mind means by Ibis,
who knows that by his deeds he has earned these prayers.
There is no delay in me: as priest I will carry out the vows that are ratified.
Whoever is present at my rites, keep holy silence;
whoever is present at my rites, speak words of mourning,
and come to Ibis with cheeks wet with weeping;
meet him with evil omens and with left feet,
and let black garments cover your bodies!
You too, why do you hesitate to put on the funeral fillets?
Already, as you see yourself, the altar of your funeral stands ready.
The procession is prepared for you. Let there be no delay to the grim vows:
give your throat to my knives, accursed victim.
May the earth deny you its crops, the river deny you its waters;
may the wind and the breeze deny their breath.
